# `scripts/post-process/pkcreader.py`

Source: [pkcreader.py](../../../../scripts/post-process/pkcreader.py)

```text
Reader for compressed pkdgrav3 snapshots (.pkc, docs/snapcomp_format.md). Needs numpy and zstandard.

Written from the format spec only, independent of the C++ code. One file, so it can be copied next to
Sahyadri's readers.py.

    from pkcreader import PkcSnapshot
    s = PkcSnapshot("snapshots/snap.00100")            # all <prefix>.s*.pkc files of one snapshot
    s.redshift, s.scale, s.Lbox, s.npart, s.mpart, s.Om, s.Olam, s.hubble, s.percents
    d = s.read(subsamples=[1, 3])                       # dict: pos (n,3) Mpc/h in [0, L), vel (n,3) km/s, ids
    d = s.read(fields=("pos", "pot"))                   # pot (n,): peculiar potential in (km/s)^2, if stored
    s.has_potential, s.pot_step
    pos = s.read_block("pos", subsamples=[1])           # SnapshotReader style: (3, n); "vel" (3, n); "ids" (n,)
    for pos, vel, ids in s.iter_blocks():               # streaming, one block (<= 65536 particles) at a time
        ...

Velocities are peculiar velocities in km/s (not Gadget's v/sqrt(a)). Subsamples are chosen by percent
(1, 3, 5, 9, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25 by default); a particle is in the same subsample in every snapshot.
Particles come out in file order, then block order; the order is the same on every call, so
read_block("pos") and read_block("ids") line up.

Lower level: PKCFile(path).header / .read(), decode_block(header, bytes), read_snapshot(prefix).
```

## parse_header

```python
parse_header(b)
```

Parse the fixed-size header of a snapcomp (.pkc) file from the bytes `b`.

Returns a dict with the grid and quantisation parameters, particle counts, box size, velocity and potential
steps (`pot_step` 0 if the file stores no potential), the info string, the cosmology (version 3) and
`q` = ncell x sub. Raises ValueError for a file that is not snapcomp or an unsupported version.

## _unzigzag

```python
_unzigzag(u)
```

Zig-zag decoding: unsigned integers back to signed (0, 1, 2, 3 -&gt; 0, -1, 1, -2).

## decode_block

```python
decode_block(h, b)
```

Decode one block: integer positions X (n,3), velocities V (n,3) in vel\_step units, IDs (n).

## decode_block_full

```python
decode_block_full(h, b)
```

As decode\_block, plus the potential P (n,) in pot\_step units (None if the file has none).

## class PKCFile

```python
class PKCFile
```

One .pkc file, memory-mapped; blocks are decoded on demand.

### PKCFile.__init__

```python
__init__(self, path)
```

Memory-map one .pkc file, check its trailer and read the header and block index.

### PKCFile.block

```python
block(self, i, pot=False)
```

(X, V, ids) of block i; with pot=True also P (potential in pot\_step units, None if absent).

### PKCFile.blocks

```python
blocks(self)
```

Yield every block of the file decoded (see `block`).

### PKCFile.read

```python
read(self, units='mpc')
```

All particles of the file: positions (`units` 'mpc': Mpc/h in [0, L); 'box': [-0.5, 0.5)),
velocities and IDs.

## read_snapshot

```python
read_snapshot(prefix, percents=None, units='mpc')
```

Read all files of one snapshot (or only the listed subsample percents) and concatenate.

## class PkcSnapshot

```python
class PkcSnapshot
```

All files of one compressed snapshot (every subsample, every writer).

### PkcSnapshot.__init__

```python
__init__(self, prefix, threads=None)
```

Open every subsample file `<prefix>.s*.pkc` of a snapshot; `threads` decode blocks in parallel.
Raises FileNotFoundError if there is none.

### PkcSnapshot._select

```python
_select(self, subsamples)
```

The files of the requested subsample percentages (all if None); ValueError if none matches.

### PkcSnapshot.count

```python
count(self, subsamples=None)
```

Number of particles in the selected subsamples.

### PkcSnapshot.read

```python
read(self, fields=('pos', 'vel', 'ids'), subsamples=None, units='mpc', dtype=np.float32)
```

Return a dict of the requested fields ("pos", "vel", "ids", "pot") for the chosen subsamples (percents).

### PkcSnapshot.read_block

```python
read_block(self, block='pos', subsamples=None)
```

SnapshotReader-style: pos and vel as (3, n), ids as (n,).

### PkcSnapshot.iter_blocks

```python
iter_blocks(self, subsamples=None, units='mpc')
```

Yield (pos (n,3), vel (n,3), ids) per block, in the same order as read().
